claims.text: Public Law 118-159, Title LXVIII, sec. 6801 ('COMPTROLLER GENERAL OF THE UNITED STATES REVIEW OF ALL-DOMAIN ANOMALY RESOLUTION OFFICE') and sec. 6802 ('SUNSET OF REQUIREMENTS RELATING TO AUDITS OF UNIDENTIFIED ANOMALOUS PHENOMENA HISTORICAL RECORD REPORT'), 138 Stat. 2520-2521. Approved 23 December 2024.

Sec. 6802 sunsets the IAA FY2023 sec. 6803 GAO briefing cadence 90 days after, and the reporting cadence 180 days after, 'the delivery of the final volume of the Historical Record Report' - tying continued GAO oversight to AARO's own delivery schedule.

Sec. 6801 requires a Comptroller General review of AARO with a report due 'in a timeframe mutually agreed upon by the congressional intelligence committees, the congressional defense committees, congressional leadership, and the Comptroller General.'
Sec. 6802 sunsets the GAO's quarterly audit information-sharing 90 days after delivery of the final volume of the Historical Record Report, and the semiannual congressional briefings 180 days after.

claims.text: Setting the report deadline by mutual agreement rather than by date leaves the timing of the only new FY2025 oversight product in the hands of the parties being overseen and their committees.

desc: Title LXVIII of the Intelligence Authorization Act for FY2025, enacted inside P.L. 118-159 on 23 December 2024, is what UAP oversight looked like in the year the disclosure bill got no vote. Sec. 6801 directs the Comptroller General to review AARO's implementation of its duties under 50 U.S.C. 3373, including its operational reporting process and its coordination with DoD, the intelligence community, other agencies and non-Government entities, and to report to the intelligence and defence committees and congressional leadership 'in a timeframe mutually agreed upon' — a deadline with no date in it. Sec. 6802 does the opposite of oversight: it amends Sec. 6803 of the IAA FY2023 to terminate the Comptroller General's quarterly information-sharing on Historical Record Report audits 90 days after the final volume is delivered, and the semiannual verbal briefings to Congress 180 days after. The FY2025 cycle therefore both commissions a new GAO look and puts an expiry on the existing one, while the disclosure regime the Senate had passed twice went unconsidered.
